summary: Creates additional SIP Resource-Priority namespaces for 3GPP Mission Critical Push To Talk and registers them with IANA.

eli5.summary: Reserving special priority labels so emergency push-to-talk calls can go first.

questions: what is mission critical push to talk
subtitle: Two new SIP priority namespaces, mcpttp and mcpttq, registered so Mission Critical Push To Talk calls can be prioritized.

tldr.problem: 3GPP's Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) service needs to prioritize calls when network resources are scarce, and the existing SIP Resource-Priority namespaces did not cover its needs.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC creates two namespaces, mcpttp (intended algorithm: preemption) and mcpttq (intended algorithm: queuing), each with priority levels 0 to 15, and registers them with IANA.
tldr.outcome: The namespaces are defined only for MCPTT services on 3GPP-defined LTE networks; use elsewhere is undefined. The document is administrative and does not affect security.

today: RFC 8101 is an Informational RFC, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the document that creates the mcpttp and mcpttq namespaces.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) has defined a Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) over LTE service. It supports group calls, where each user gains permission to talk in an arbitrated manner, and private calls between pairs of users. It targets professional users such as public safety, transport companies, utilities, and industrial and nuclear plants, and a commercial service may also be delivered through an MCPTT system.

MCPTT gives users different priorities for access to network resources so calls can be prioritized when resources are scarce. The priorities take into account the caller's priority and role, the group's priority and type, and the situation in which the call is made.
sections.eli5: MCPTT is a walkie-talkie service over the phone network for people like emergency workers. When the network is crowded, important calls need to win.

sections.title: Preemption and Queuing
sections.content:
High-priority calls, such as when the life of a public safety worker or anyone else is in danger, must be set up immediately, so they require preemption. Other calls may be less sensitive to setup time but have a high priority once established, so a queueing mechanism fits better. The RFC gives the MCPTT data transfer service and video-only calls as examples that can benefit from queueing.

This is why two namespaces are needed. The SIP-level call control procedures that use them are specified in 3GPP TS 24.379, and operators can tailor usage by configuring which values a given user may use.
sections.eli5: An emergency call is like an ambulance that pushes ahead of traffic. A less urgent call is like waiting in a line, but once you are in, nobody should kick you out.

sections.title: Applicability
sections.content:
The namespaces apply to MCPTT services defined by 3GPP that use the network services of a 3GPP-defined LTE network. The RFC states that use outside such networks is undefined.

The namespaces are also described as corresponding to what can be supported over the 3GPP Rx interface, and as supporting a wide range of queuing options.
sections.eli5: These labels are made for one kind of phone network. Using them anywhere else is not covered.

sections.title: The Two Namespaces
sections.content:
The mcpttp namespace has priority levels mcpttp.0 (lowest) through mcpttp.15 (highest). Its Namespace Numerical Value is 46 and its intended algorithm is preemption.

The mcpttq namespace has levels mcpttq.0 (lowest) through mcpttq.15 (highest). Its Namespace Numerical Value is 47 and its intended algorithm is queuing.

For both, the RFC says there is no new Warning code and no new SIP response code.
sections.eli5: There are two ladders, each with steps from 0 to 15. Higher steps win. One ladder is for pushing ahead and the other is for waiting your turn.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
Following the rules of RFC 4412 and RFC 7134, the RFC is an Informational RFC that creates two new namespaces, their priority values and their intended algorithms in the IANA registry.

On security, the RFC says it has no impact on the security of the SIP MCPTT protocol and that its purpose is purely administrative.
sections.eli5: The RFC just writes the new labels into the official list. It does not change how safe anything is.
